label: Acts 14:1
text: In Iconium, they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spoke that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.

label: Acts 14:2
text: But the disbelieving Jews stirred up and embittered the souls of the Gentiles against the brothers.

label: Acts 14:3
text: Therefore they stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who testified to the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.

label: Acts 14:4
text: But the multitude of the city was divided. Part sided with the Jews, and part with the apostles.

label: Acts 14:5
text: When some of both the Gentiles and the Jews, with their rulers, made a violent attempt to mistreat and stone them,

label: Acts 14:6
text: they became aware of it, and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and the surrounding region.

label: Acts 14:7
text: There they preached the Good News.

label: Acts 14:8
text: At Lystra a certain man sat, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.

label: Acts 14:9
text: He was listening to Paul speaking, who, fastening eyes on him, and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,

label: Acts 14:10
text: said with a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” He leaped up and walked.

label: Acts 14:11
text: When the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”

label: Acts 14:12
text: They called Barnabas “Jupiter”, and Paul “Mercury”, because he was the chief speaker.

label: Acts 14:13
text: The priest of Jupiter, whose temple was in front of their city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and would have made a sacrifice along with the multitudes.

label: Acts 14:14
text: But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of it, they tore their clothes, and sprang into the multitude, crying out,

label: Acts 14:15
text: “Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made the sky, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them;

label: Acts 14:16
text: who in the generations gone by allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways.

label: Acts 14:17
text: Yet he didn’t leave himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you rains from the sky and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.”

label: Acts 14:18
text: Even saying these things, they hardly stopped the multitudes from making a sacrifice to them.

label: Acts 14:19
text: But some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there, and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul, and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.

label: Acts 14:20
text: But as the disciples stood around him, he rose up, and entered into the city. On the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.

label: Acts 14:21
text: When they had preached the Good News to that city, and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,

label: Acts 14:22
text: confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many afflictions we must enter into God’s Kingdom.

label: Acts 14:23
text: When they had appointed elders for them in every assembly, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they had believed.

label: Acts 14:24
text: They passed through Pisidia, and came to Pamphylia.

label: Acts 14:25
text: When they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

label: Acts 14:26
text: From there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.

label: Acts 14:27
text: When they had arrived, and had gathered the assembly together, they reported all the things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith to the nations.

label: Acts 14:28
text: They stayed there with the disciples for a long time.

label: Synagogue preaching at Iconium
statement: Paul and Barnabas entered the Jewish synagogue at Iconium and spoke so that a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks believed.

label: Opposition and stoning attempt at Iconium
statement: At Iconium disbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles; the city was divided, and Jews and Gentiles with their rulers attempted to mistreat and stone Paul and Barnabas.

label: Flight to the Lycaonian cities Lystra and Derbe
statement: Paul and Barnabas fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding region.
note: Derbe's regional assignment varies in ancient sources: Strabo puts it 'on the side of the Isaurian territory close upon Cappadocia' (fetched Perseus 12.6.3) and the fetched Wikipedia Derbe article adds that Stephanus of Byzantium places it in Isauria, while it was in Lycaonia when Paul and Barnabas visited. Kind corrected from place to event in consolidation B: the statement is an event (the matrix anchors office/event/object/custom/time claims).

label: Paul heals the cripple at Lystra
statement: At Lystra Paul healed a man lame from birth, who had never walked, and he leaped up and walked.
note: Miracle claim; searched honestly and recorded none-found in every external category. Setting evidence for Lystra is kept separate and never graded as attesting the healing.

label: Lystran crowd: the gods have come down
statement: The Lystran crowd lifted up its voice and called out that the gods had come down to them in the likeness of men.

label: The Lycaonian language of the crowd
statement: The Lystran crowd spoke in the local language of Lycaonia rather than Greek.
note: The Lycaonian language itself is unattested: the fetched Wikipedia Lycaonian language article classifies it as 'an unclassified extinct language' (unattested), and the fetched Acts 14 article says 'ancient inscriptions confirm' the pre-Greek language without naming any inscription on the page.

label: Barnabas called Zeus, Paul called Hermes
statement: The Lystrans called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, because Paul was the chief speaker. (The WEB translates the Greek Zeus and Hermes as Jupiter and Mercury.)

label: The priest of Zeus and the sacrifice
statement: The priest of Zeus at Lystra, whose temple stood in front of the city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates to sacrifice with the crowds.
note: The temple 'in front of the city' (pro tes poleos) is not stated on any fetched page; only the existence of priests of Zeus at Lystra is externally attested (1909 inscriptions).

label: Jews from Antioch and Iconium stone Paul
statement: Jews from Antioch and Iconium came to Lystra, persuaded the crowds, stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.

label: Return visit and appointment of elders
statement: Returning through Lystra, Iconium and Pisidian Antioch, Paul and Barnabas strengthened the disciples and appointed elders for them in every church with prayer and fasting.

label: Through Pisidia and Pamphylia to Perga
statement: They passed through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia, and spoke the word in Perga.

label: Down to Attalia
statement: From Perga they went down to Attalia, the coastal city of Pamphylia.

label: Sail to Antioch in Syria and report
statement: From Attalia they sailed to Antioch in Syria, reported to the church what God had done with them, and stayed a long time with the disciples.
